renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  id: filter_partition
  title: Calls by FILTER value per caller
  description: |-
    Each bar is a caller, stacked by the FILTER value its calls carry, with the number of variants in each. It answers what each caller keeps and what it flags as filtered.
    How to read: a bar that is mostly PASS means a caller that keeps most of its calls. A large share under another label shows what the caller's own filters remove, and a caller that applies no filter shows a single segment. Compare shares and not heights, since callers differ in the number of calls.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: caller
    y: n_variants
    color: filter_label
    barmode: stack
    labels:
      caller: Caller
      n_variants: Variants
      filter_label: FILTER value

- component: card
  title: Calls by FILTER value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of calls across the callers in view, and the ring splits them by FILTER value. It answers what share of the calls pass the callers' own filters.
    How to read: a ring that is mostly PASS means the filters remove little. A large slice of another label is what the callers discard, so check its Ts/Tv in the table to see whether the removed calls look like noise.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html
  column: n_variants
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: filter_label
  caption: calls, by FILTER value

- component: card
  title: Calls by caller
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of calls, and the bars rank the callers by how many calls they made. It answers which caller is the most and the least productive.
    How to read: a caller far ahead may be more sensitive or less strict, so read the count with its Ts/Tv and its share of PASS calls.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html
  column: n_variants
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: caller
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: calls, by caller

- component: card
  title: Ts/Tv of kept calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median transition to transversion ratio of the calls that carry PASS or no filter, and the box shows the spread across callers and samples. It answers whether the kept calls have the balance expected of real variants.
    How to read: false calls are spread evenly over bases, so they pull the ratio down. A caller whose kept calls sit below the others adds noise, and the expected value depends on the genome region sequenced, whole genome or exome.
    Note: the tool publishes no cut-off for the ratio, so none is drawn.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25297068/
  column: ts_tv
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  filter_expr: col('filter_label').is_in(['PASS', '.'])
  caption: kept calls, median with its spread

- component: table
  title: FILTER summary table
  description: |-
    Each row is a caller and a FILTER value, with the number of calls, how many are transitions and transversions, their ratio and their share of the callset. It answers the exact numbers behind each tile.
    How to read: compare the Ts/Tv of the rejected labels with PASS to see whether a filter removes noise or good calls.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tstv_quality_sweep
  title: Ts/Tv by quality threshold
  description: |-
    Each curve is a sample and caller: the transition to transversion ratio of the SNPs whose quality is above each threshold. It answers whether raising the quality floor makes the calls more like real variants.
    How to read: a ratio that rises with the threshold means quality separates real from false calls, and a curve that stays flat means the quality score carries no information. The level to expect depends on the genome region sequenced, so compare callers on the same data.
    Note: the tool publishes no ideal ratio, so no reference line is drawn. Only bi-allelic SNPs are counted.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25297068/
  kind: profile
  config:
    x_title: Minimum quality score
    y_title: Ts/Tv of the calls above it
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    series: series
    x: qual_threshold
    y: ts_tv_above

- component: figure
  title: Ts/Tv by quality, static view
  description: |-
    Each line is a sample and caller: the Ts/Tv ratio of the calls above each quality threshold. It answers the same question as the interactive sweep, in a plain figure that can be exported.
    How to read: a line that climbs and levels off marks the quality score from which extra filtering gains little.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html
  visu_type: line
  dict_kwargs:
    x: qual_threshold
    y: ts_tv_above
    color: series
    labels:
      qual_threshold: Minimum quality score
      ts_tv_above: Ts/Tv of the calls above it
      series: Sample and caller

- component: card
  title: Ts/Tv across the sweep
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median Ts/Tv ratio over every quality threshold and series in view, and the box shows the spread. It answers the typical balance of transitions and transversions of the callsets.
    How to read: callsets with a lower box add more noise. Filter to one caller to read its own level.
    Note: the tool publishes no ideal ratio, which depends on the genome region.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25297068/
  column: ts_tv_above
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median over the sweep, with its spread

- component: table
  title: Ts/Tv sweep table
  description: |-
    Each row is a quality threshold of a sample and caller, with the transitions and transversions above it and their ratio. It answers the exact numbers behind the curves.
    How to read: filter by series and read down the thresholds to see where the ratio stops improving.
    Source: https://vcftools.github.io/man_latest.html
